classification.difficultyReason: Convert the northwest bearing to an acute triangle angle, distinguish westward displacement from journey length and choose suitable ratios for the hypotenuse and northward distance.

content.prompt: A ship travels on a bearing of $320^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ until it is $50\text{ km}$ west of its starting point.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How far did it travel? Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
The ship travels northwest, making an angle of $360^{\circ}-320^{\circ}=40^{\circ}$ with north. Let $d$ kilometres be the distance travelled. The westward displacement is opposite this angle.
$$\begin{align*}\sin40^{\circ}&=\frac{50}{d}\\d\sin40^{\circ}&=50\\d&=\frac{50}{\sin40^{\circ}}\\d&\approx77.8\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How far north of its starting point is it? Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
Let $n$ kilometres be the northward displacement. The angle between the journey and north is $40^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan40^{\circ}&=\frac{50}{n}\\n\tan40^{\circ}&=50\\n&=\frac{50}{\tan40^{\circ}}\\n&\approx59.6\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
The ship is $59.6\text{ km}$ north of its starting point.
